findings.title: Pressure that crosses a stopping point
findings.claim: The prohibition presents religious excess as pressure that goes beyond a stopping point: the focus form is heard with the images of boiling over, reaching a limit, and exceeding a furthest range.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier at 5:77:5:1 contacts the adjacent stopping form at 5:73:17 and the mutual-restraint form at 5:79:3. Those independent limit contacts make the nominated boiling, endpoint, overstepping, and farthest-reach facets explain how excess moves across a boundary rather than merely naming a large amount.
findings.reader_payoff: The warning becomes a discernible movement with a stopping point, so the reader can perceive both the intensity of overreach and the boundary it crosses.
findings.containment: This is a pericope-local pressure image attached to the supplied focus occurrence. It does not claim a literal boiling vessel or arrow in the ayah, and it does not settle any wider recurrence. The غ ل و carrier mapping is retained as qualified supplied evidence.

epistemic.reason: The channel evidence and context roots are trusted, but the nominated غ ل و branch identity is not independently aligned with the focus surface row's غ ل ل root record.

findings.title: Desire falls away from the even road
findings.claim: The warning lets desire appear as a directional force: when a group's preferred impulses are followed, the even middle of the road becomes a route from which the group can fall, stray, and become lost.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers for أَهْوَاء, سَوَاءِ, السَّبِيلِ, and the three straying verbs meet one another within the same final warning. The road and its even middle give desire a direction, while the straying and loss facets turn following those desires into departure from orientation and possession.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the sentence as a movement from preference through pursuit to falling away from a balanced route, while retaining the plain warning against following a misguiding group's desires.
findings.containment: The picture is local to the focus wording. It does not replace the ordinary meanings of desires, straying, or path, and it does not claim a literal traveler, animal, or physical fall.

epistemic.reason: The channel source and focus carriers are trusted; the evenness branch and falling branch carry qualified lexicon identities, so the composite movement remains explicitly qualified.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace supplies exact focus and context coordinates but is legacy_unbound; the three focus branch records are available while the context branch records are unresolved.

findings.title: A receptive route through the named group
findings.claim: The named group is made functional by a reception posture: preference-led following can be reversed by hearing, recognizing truth, and seeking entry into a witnessing and sound community.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers at 5:77:12:1 and 5:77:13:1 meet the later sequence at 5:82:26, 5:83:2, 5:83:9, 5:83:13, 5:83:15, 5:83:19, 5:83:21, 5:84:15, and 5:84:16. Non-arrogance opens hearing, hearing opens recognition, recognition leads to a request for inscription among witnesses, and the later community is qualified by soundness; this changes the group from an immutable label into a posture and possible affiliation without erasing the warning.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see how the focus's group-language leaves room for a change of reception and belonging: the danger is carried by a way of responding, while another response can seek a different company.
findings.containment: The later sequence supplies an attributed contextual contrast, not a redefinition of every use of قوم or أهواء. It does not identify the focus group with the later responders, and it does not make the later subgroup a universal rule.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace has exact supplied anchors and roles but legacy_unbound provenance; unresolved context branches are preserved as attributed rather than lexically confirmed.

findings.title: An accountable religious order
findings.claim: When the focus's دِينِكُمْ meets the added phrase يوم الدِّين, the religious order in which excess occurs also carries an accountability horizon: its judgments and returns remain answerable while the local prohibition stays intact.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier at 5:77:7:1 meets the independent external scene at 1:4:1-1:4:2, where ownership and a bounded day frame the supplied judgment-and-recompense facet of dīn. That contact adds answerability to the focus's religious-domain reading without replacing it with the name of a particular day.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the focus's religious domain as an order with consequences and answerability, not only as a community possession.
findings.containment: The added line supplies a bounded overlay through the focus word; it does not claim that 5:77 directly names the Day of Recompense, and it does not use the overlay to decide the focus's plain meaning.

epistemic.reason: The contact is grounded in exact supplied focus and external root occurrences, while the semantic synthesis across the added line is an authoring inference without a dedicated support record.
